A systemd timer that runs a command on a schedule.

```hcl
step "example" {
  timer {
    command = "..."
    name = "..."
    on_calendar = "..."
  }
}
```

## Arguments

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `command` | string | Yes | Command to run (ExecStart). |
| `description` | string | No | Unit description. |
| `name` | string | Yes | Unit name, without .timer or .service. |
| `on_calendar` | string | Yes | systemd calendar expression, such as "daily" or "*-*-* 02:30:00". |
| `on_remove` | string | No | "delete" (default) stops the timer and removes its units, "forget" leaves it. |
| `persistent` | bool | No | Run a missed job at the next boot. |
| `user` | string | No | User the command runs as. Defaults to root. |

## Read-only attributes

Conn3x sets these; reference them as `conn3x_timer.<circuit>__<step>["<host>"].<name>`.

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `in_sync` | bool | Whether the units match and the timer is enabled and running. |

A step lowers to the `conn3x_timer` resource, one instance per host, and connects with its circuit's `ssh` block.
